mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to increased borrowing costs and reduced corporate investments, which in turn depresses S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower in tightening periods compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within the last month indicates weakening labor market conditions, which leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower in periods of rising unemployment compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in real estate sales (HOUST) signals a weakening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of broader economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower during periods of declining housing sales compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% within the last month signals a contraction in the supply side of the economy, leading to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly lower in periods of declining industrial production compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is above 7% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) decreases by more than 100,000 in the last month, it signals a significant labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 7% and PAYEMS decreases > 100,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower in periods of high unemployment and declining employment compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow by less than 0.5% month-over-month and CPI (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5%, it signals stagflationary pressures, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS growth < 0.5% MoM and CPIAUCSL > 0.5% MoM
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower in periods of low consumption growth and high inflation compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 1% signals a strong tightening cycle, leading to increased borrowing costs and reduced corporate investments, which depresses S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower in tightening periods compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) increases by more than 2% in the last quarter and GDP (GDPC1) grows by more than 1%, it signals a strong economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases > 2% in 3 months and GDPC1 > 1%
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher in periods of strong industrial production and GDP growth compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
